the evidence for statin efficacy and safety is dose‐dependent.

statin dose is important, that statin doses above five‐fold estimated effective dose (ED50) have no clinical benefit and that statins should be prescribed at doses of around 10 mg of simvastatin, 20 mg of pravastatin and 40 mg of fluvastatin.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the statin dose should be the lowest dose that is clinically effective, and that is usually the estimated ED50.
statin doses around ED50 are the optimal doses, and that higher doses do not confer any additional benefit, whilst increasing the risk of side‐effects.

the statin doses that have been shown to lower coronary mortality and increase survival are around the ED50, and that doses above this level have no proven benefits, but have a greater likelihood of causing adverse events.
